provenance.note: Every response body shape the live bidding workflows actually sent, measured from workflow_executions.response_body on 2026-08-21. 300 most recent non-test executions per workflow, grouped by their sorted top-level key set, with exact counts. The declarations in engine/response-contracts.ts are seeded from THIS, not written from memory, because a contract invented at the keyboard is how #926 shipped a guard reading a field nobody sends (L48).
provenance.method: 300 most recent non-test executions per workflow with a non-null response_body, grouped by sorted top-level keys
provenance.limitation: 300 rows per workflow is a recent slice, not the whole retained window, so a rare response family could be absent. That is why a body matching no declared family is reported as unrecognised rather than treated as a violation: the first thing to check is whether it is a family nobody declared.

findings.note: Two things the measurement itself turned up, recorded so they are not rediscovered.
items: Lead Economy sent 2 responses shaped { error, trace_id }. trace_id is OUR identifier, not the partner's, so a partner receiving one cannot tie it back to the lead they sent. This is the same defect #933 is about, on the internal-error path rather than a rejection path, and it is why an unrecognised family is worth reporting.

The offer family carries no lead_id and no status, so a flat 'every response must contain lead_id and status' contract would be false for it. The invariant is per family, which is why the declaration is shaped that way.
